east_texas.headline: One more warm morning, then a dry cold front this afternoon and a chilly Thanksgiving week.
east_texas.summary: A cold front moves through the Tyler area early this afternoon. Highs reach the low 70s around midday, then temperatures fall with a northwest wind gusting 20 to 25 mph. Little or no rain is expected here. A second front Tuesday night brings colder air, with lows near freezing Wednesday through Friday mornings.
east_texas.rain_note: Rain chance near 20% this morning, then dry. NWS expects a tenth of an inch or less.

days.text: Mostly sunny and cooler. Northeast wind 5 to 10 mph.
Mostly sunny and chilly. A second front arrives at night with little moisture.
Sunny. Lows near freezing, with frost in rural cold spots.
Sunny and dry. Another cold morning Friday.
Mostly sunny and a little milder. Warming into the weekend.

facts.p: Any strong storms stay over South Arkansas and North Louisiana
No outages listed in Smith or nearby counties
NWS forecasts lows near 32; rural cold spots coldest

panels.title: Colder, with several frosty mornings
paras: NWS Shreveport says temperatures return to late-November normals Monday, then a stronger system Tuesday night reinforces the cold air. It calls consecutive sub-freezing mornings very probable across northern parts of the region from Wednesday through Thanksgiving and beyond. Around Tyler, lows in the low to mid 30s are most likely, colder in rural low spots.
The Climate Prediction Center favors below-normal temperatures in East Texas for Nov 26–30, then a warmer pattern for most of the country Nov 28 – Dec 4.

panels.title: A very strong El Niño
paras: The Climate Prediction Center says El Niño is strong to very strong, near +2.5°C in the key Pacific region, with a chance of a record event this winter.

NWS Fort Worth notes that El Niño has little effect on North Texas weather until after the New Year, and a strongly negative Pacific Decadal Oscillation may keep this winter drier than a typical El Niño.

east_texas.sources: NWS Shreveport forecast and discussion, NWS Fort Worth, NOAA Storm Prediction Center, NOAA Climate Prediction Center, Texas A&M Forest Service, PowerOutage.us.

nm.headline: A frigid start, then another round of mountain snow showers Monday afternoon into Tuesday.
nm.summary: Clear, calm skies brought the coldest morning of the season, with Angel Fire near 10 degrees before sunrise. Today is sunny and chilly with high clouds later. A quick system brings rain and snow showers to the northern half of the state Monday afternoon into Tuesday morning. NWS Albuquerque expects a few inches above 9,000 feet and under an inch in the highlands. Dry weather follows for the rest of the week.

days.text: Snow showers develop in the afternoon and continue into Monday night. Slick travel possible on mountain roads.
Early snow showers end, then sunny and colder. Teens at night in the high valleys.
Sunny and dry under northwest flow.
A weak, mostly dry trough may pass. Temperatures a few degrees above normal.

nm.snow_note: Readings from the start of today. Saturday's snow added a few inches at Gallegos Peak and Taos Powderhorn.
nm.ski_note: Sipapu is open with 1 of 6 lifts and 1 trail. Its base includes man-made snow. Red River, Taos and Ski Santa Fe open this week if projections hold. Dates with ~ are projected and may change.

panels.title: Coldest morning so far, more snow Monday
paras: NWS Albuquerque says lows this morning reached the teens and 20s across central and northern New Mexico, the coldest of the season. Angel Fire fell to about 10 degrees under clear, calm skies.

A neutrally tilted trough reaches the southern Rockies Monday and pulls in some Gulf moisture. Expect rain and mountain snow showers Monday afternoon into Tuesday morning, mainly in the northern half of the state, with a few inches above 9,000 feet.

panels.title: Slick spots on US-64 near Eagle Nest
paras: NMRoads listed US-64 from east of Taos to west of Eagle Nest as snow packed and icy after Saturday's snow, along with NM-475 and parts of US-64 near Tierra Amarilla. I-25 at Raton Pass had wet and icy spots.
Monday night's snow showers can make passes and shaded canyons slick again. No fire weather concerns this week.

panels.title: Dry after Tuesday, warming late week
paras: NWS Albuquerque expects dry northwest flow from Tuesday night through the weekend, with temperatures rising a few degrees above normal by late week. The Climate Prediction Center favors above-normal temperatures for New Mexico into early December.
El Niño is very strong. It often sends more storms across the southern Rockies later in winter, though it does not guarantee a snowy season.

nm.sources: NWS Albuquerque forecast and discussion, NRCS SNOTEL, NMRoads, OnTheSnow, NOAA Climate Prediction Center.
